findings.desc: B-9958 smoke does not directly prove default dry-run no-write behavior for the mutating writer surfaces. The smoke snapshots observe/no-mutation and checks drift failure writes no proposals, but it never snapshots stores around playbook_seed_propose_batch without apply, playbook_candidate_batch_approve without apply, or playbook_auto_promotion_apply dry-run. A regression that creates proposals/candidates or mutates learning state during default dry-run could slip while the current apply-path assertions still pass.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by adding explicit store snapshot assertions proving default dry-run/no-apply paths for playbook_seed_propose_batch, playbook_candidate_batch_approve, and playbook_auto_promotion_apply do not mutate proposals, candidates, outcomes, decisions, or non_promotable registry; verified by node packages/main/dist/tasks/playbook-seed-promotion-loop-smoke.js.

findings.desc: B-9958 lacks enough CLI-level coverage for the new command surfaces and undercovers M7 status/readiness. The recorded smoke invokes createPlaybookHandlers directly and checks MAIN_TOOLS/COMMAND_POLICIES/PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS membership, but it does not execute the actual lattice CLI for the CLI-marked verification intents, nor does it call playbook_promotion_status to assert the V1 readiness and V2 disabled posture promised by CHK-005. CLI parser/schema/default flag behavior and status text/json output could regress without this smoke failing.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by executing actual built CLI surfaces in the smoke, including playbook_promotion_status JSON/text readiness and V2 disabled posture; verified by node packages/main/dist/tasks/playbook-seed-promotion-loop-smoke.js and command catalog/ownership smokes.

findings.desc: Command docs/catalog surfaces still lead with legacy non-deducible wording instead of the B-9958 canonical non_promotable wording. The decision doc establishes non_promotable as the operator-facing term and says legacy non_deducible / mark_non_deducible are compatibility spellings (docs/requirements/decisions/source-lineage-dedup-playbook-seed-promotion-execution-plan.md:157-161), and the text status renderer adds non_promotableSources with legacy storage noted (packages/main/src/handlers/playbook.ts:1116-1118). However playbook_promotion_status help/catalog still renders non-deducible sources (packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:1878), command-policy still says non-deducible source registry (packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:246), and process-fact levels still say non-deducible sources (packages/main/src/core/process-fact-levels.ts:156). This leaves the changed docs/catalog output inconsistent with the B-9958 terminology requirement; update these surfaces to lead with non_promotable while explicitly noting legacy non_deducible storage.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed command catalog, command policy, and process fact wording to lead with canonical non_promotable terminology while noting legacy non_deducible storage compatibility only where needed.

findings.desc: New read-only playbook commands are missing from READ_ONLY_COMMANDS, so invoking playbook_seed_observe or playbook_runtime_consumption_verify through the CLI still runs preCommand/postCommand hooks and appends .lattice/activity.jsonl by default. Both commands are declared readOnly in COMMAND_POLICIES and L0 in PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS, and their handlers assert no write/apply flags, but cli-engine.ts gates hook execution and shouldWriteActivityLog on cli/activity-policy.ts READ_ONLY_COMMANDS. Because the new read-only names were not added there, the documented read-only/non-mutating guarantee is false for normal CLI execution and reviewer read-only mode can still trigger hook side effects.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by registering playbook_seed_observe and playbook_runtime_consumption_verify as read-only activity-policy commands so read-only diagnostics are not incorrectly owner-gated as mutating actions; verified by command ownership contract smoke.

findings.desc: Finding-signal seeds are treated as proposable based only on example IDs and lineage. source-lineage-audit.ts:270-291 projects every signal with exampleFindingIds/storyIds into finding_signal records, and playbook-seed.ts:434-490 only blocks missing lineage, already represented sources, or non_promotable sources. The execution plan requires finding-signals to have support above a configured threshold and valid anchors before they can become proposal material. As implemented, a low-support or anchorless signal with one exampleFindingId can pass observe/propose and become an inert candidate, so the seed loop is not actually threshold-gated.

Batch candidate approval does not preserve the canonical-source dedup boundary. buildCandidateManifestRows records each proposal canonicalSourceKey in manifest rows, but buildPlaybookCandidateBatchManifest apply only checks the manifest digest, invalid proposal list, and duplicate candidate IDs before writing all candidates. It does not reject duplicate canonicalSourceKey rows in the manifest or re-run source_lineage_audit to ensure another proposal/playbook for the same canonical source has not appeared. Duplicate seed proposals can therefore be approved into multiple candidate playbooks for the same source, undercutting the acceptance criterion that one canonical source cannot silently create multiple proposal/candidate paths.

B-9958 still treats stale finding-signal anchors as valid seed material. collectFindingSignals copies any non-empty anchorFiles into anchorRefs without checking whether the anchors still exist or pass the existing revalidation contract (packages/main/src/core/source-lineage-audit.ts:281-305), and findingSignalQualityBlockReasons only blocks finding_signal records when anchorRefs is empty (packages/main/src/core/playbook-seed.ts:395-401). The repo already defines valid anchored signals as having at least one present anchor file, with all-missing anchors classified as stale (packages/main/src/core/experience-revalidation.ts:46-77), and the B-9958 plan requires finding-signals to have support above threshold and valid anchors (docs/requirements/decisions/source-lineage-dedup-playbook-seed-promotion-execution-plan.md:145-146). A signal with support >= 1 and anchorFiles=["no/such/file.ts"] can therefore pass observe/propose as proposable even though its anchors are stale, so F-005 is only partially fixed and anchor quality does not fail closed.

F-003 is only partially fixed: the catalog/policy/fact-level wording now leads with non_promotable, but playbook_promotion_status still exposes legacy non_deducible wording as operator-visible status output. The decision doc says non_promotable is canonical and non_deducible / mark_non_deducible are legacy compatibility spellings (docs/requirements/decisions/source-lineage-dedup-playbook-seed-promotion-execution-plan.md:157-161). Current status JSON still uses nonDeducibleSources and paths.nonDeducibleSources, and the text renderer prints nonDeducibleSources before non_promotableSources (packages/main/src/handlers/playbook.ts:1060-1096,1116-1118). This keeps the actual CLI status surface out of sync with the B-9958 wording boundary; keep legacy storage names if needed, but expose canonical nonPromotable/non_promotable wording in status output with legacy storage noted only parenthetically.

F-008 fixed the direct playbook_promotion_status surface: status JSON now exposes nonPromotableSources/paths.nonPromotableSources and the text renderer prints nonPromotableSources with legacy storage noted parenthetically. However adjacent docs/prose still present the legacy non_deducible terminology outside the allowed legacy-storage compatibility boundary. The B-9958 source-lineage plan makes non_promotable canonical and limits non_deducible / mark_non_deducible to compatibility spellings, but docs/requirements/decisions/playbook-promotion-worker-execution-plan.md still describes operator-visible state/output/acceptance as non_deducible or non-deducible sources at lines 185, 188, 656, 672, 815, 932-942, 966, and 974. The policy/fact rationale for playbook_promotion_sweep also says non-deducible metadata rather than non_promotable source registry with legacy storage noted (packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:244, packages/main/src/core/process-fact-levels.ts:154). This leaves docs surfaces inconsistent with the round-3 boundary that non_deducible should appear only as legacy storage compatibility wording/path.
